Elena / team —

Thanks for the clarity. I drafted two short options below so ClearWave can pick the one that maps to their risk profile. Both are intentionally concise so procurement can sign quickly; we can expand in a SOW if needed.

Option A — Contract-level commitment (recommended for enterprise):
"Redwood will provide exportable audit logs capturing press-related approvals and related metadata (approver name, role, approval timestamp, and asset reference). Such logs will be retained for a period of twelve (12) months following approval and made available to Customer upon request within five (5) business days."

Option B — Operational commitment (lower contractual exposure):
"Redwood’s Console and Designated Customer Admins will maintain an approval log for publicity assets; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide exported evidence upon request and will retain approval artifacts in accordance with its operational retention policy."

Embargo carve-out suggestion (add to publicity clause):
"Customer may designate an embargo window not to exceed ninety (90) days, during which Customer may delay public disclosure of Launch Materials. Redwood will not publicize Customer’s name, logo, or Confidential Information during the embargo unless Customer issues written approval."

Notes:
- Option A is straightforward but requires us to treat exportability and specific retention as a contractual obligation.
- Option B keeps us flexible operationally but may not satisfy procurement/legal teams that require auditable guarantees.

Ben — once you confirm which option aligns with our pricing/commitment levels, I’ll incorporate the language into OrderForm_v3 and circulate for final sign-off.

Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
